definitions.type: integer-valued family indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For natural j, c_j is the integer cast of Nat.choose(λ.toNat,j). For λ≥0 this is binom(λ,j).
D=∏_(t=0)^(λ.toNat) c_t; an empty product is one.

inputs.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.
For a prime p, a ring A with CharP A p, and n∈N, the element n! cast to A is a unit if and only if n<p.

hypotheses: p is a prime natural number.
A has characteristic p in the CharP sense.
source_contract.signature:
@IsUnit.natCast_factorial_iff_of_charP : ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring.{u_1} A] (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP.{u_1} A p] {n : ℕ},
  IsUnit.{u_1} ↑n.factorial ↔ LT.lt.{0} n p

inputs.statement: For natural numbers n,k with k≤n, choose(n,k)·k!·(n−k)!=n!.

hypotheses: n and k are natural numbers.
source_contract.signature:
@Nat.choose_mul_factorial_mul_factorial : ∀ {n k : ℕ},
  LE.le.{0} k n →
    Eq.{1} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (n.choose k) k.factorial) (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} n k).factorial)
      n.factorial

output.statement: For every j with 0≤j≤λ the integer c_j=binom(λ,j) has nonzero image in K; for every r with 0≤r≤λ the integer r! has nonzero image in K. Hence D=∏_(j=0)^λ c_j also has nonzero image in K.

argument.text: For every natural r≤λ, H001 gives r<p. Apply M004 with ring K, its characteristic p from H001, and source natural n=r. The right side of its equivalence holds, so r! cast into K is a unit and hence nonzero in the field K. This includes r=0, whose factorial is one.

produces.statement: For every natural r≤λ, (r! in K) is nonzero.

argument.text: For every natural j≤λ, apply M005 with source n=λ.toNat and k=j. Cast its identity c_j j!(λ−j)!=λ! into K. Since λ! is nonzero by F001, the left side is nonzero; if c_j had zero image its product would be zero. Thus every c_j has nonzero image. A finite product of nonzero elements of a field is nonzero, by induction on the number of factors and the absence of zero divisors. D is precisely that product, so its image is nonzero. This proves the output statement with the factorial statement F001.

applications.bindings: Take source ring A=K, its prime=p, and its natural number n=r for each natural r≤λ.
hypothesis_checks: K is a field by H001 and therefore a ring.
H001 gives characteristic p for K, which is the CharP condition.
The quantified r is a natural number. H001 additionally gives r≤λ

applications.bindings: Take source natural n=λ.toNat and k=j, for every natural j≤λ.
hypothesis_checks: H001 gives λ≥0, so λ.toNat represents λ, and j is natural.

statement_closure.notes: The prime and characteristic conditions and 0≤λ

background_notes.fact: Set n=λ.toNat. Under H001, the integer cast of n equals λ and n<p. For natural r with integer cast r≤λ, r≤n and r<p. In particular n itself is an allowed instance of F001 in S002; any natural j≤λ also satisfies j≤n.

grounds.reason: Gives 0≤λ
Uses arbitrary natural r≤λ.

background_notes.justification: A nonnegative integer is the integer cast of its natural representative. Natural-to-integer casting preserves and reflects order, so the stated index comparisons and r

background_notes.fact: For n=λ.toNat and j≤n, casting M005 into K gives (c_j in K)·(j! in K)·((n−j)! in K)=(n! in K). The image of D equals ∏_{t=0}^{n}(c_t in K).

grounds.reason: K is a field, so its canonical natural and integer casts exist.
Provides the natural factorial identity for j≤n.
Defines c_j as the integer cast of choose(n,j).
Defines D as the finite integer product of c_t.

background_notes.justification: The canonical casts preserve 1, addition and multiplication, and the natural cast agrees with composition through the integers. Applying these maps preserves the factorial identity, and induction on the finite number of factors preserves the defining product for D. Because j≤n, the notation λ−j in the prose represents the same nonnegative subtraction n−j.

background_notes.fact: In K every unit is nonzero, and a finite product of nonzero elements is nonzero. A product containing a zero factor is zero. These facts apply respectively to the units in S001, the coefficient identity in S002, and the finite product defining D.

grounds.reason: K is a field, with 1≠0 and inverses for nonzero elements.
M004 establishes the factorial units in S001.
The factorial identity and F001 establish coefficient nonvanishing before the product argument.
D has finitely many indexed factors.

background_notes.justification: A unit equal to zero would give 1=0 upon multiplication by its inverse. If a,b≠0 and ab=0, multiplying by a inverse gives b=0, a contradiction. Induction starting with the empty product 1 proves the finite-product assertion. The zero-factor assertion follows from multiplication by zero and associativity. These supply the routine field reasoning already used in the two paragraphs.
